column1: # The stock ASP.NET Core templates, and what AuthzProbe should say about each.
# These are real applications written by Microsoft, not fixtures written to make the tool
# look good, which is the point: a rule that is wrong about the framework's own idioms is
# wrong about everybody's code.
# max_analysed is the regression guard that matters. MapStaticAssets registers one endpoint
# per file, and a stock MVC application once produced 385 findings, 380 of them about
# bootstrap.css, while every unit test stayed green.
# The templates differ between framework versions — .NET 8 serves static files with
# middleware, .NET 10 with endpoints — so expectations are recorded per framework.
# That difference is also the best evidence that excluding static assets is right rather
# than convenient: .NET 8 never registers them as endpoints at all, and once .NET 10's are
# excluded the two frameworks report identical numbers for every template below. The
# exclusion recovers the surface .NET 8 shows natively.
# framework  name                template  extra                max_analysed  errors  warnings  infos
net10.0      webapi-minimal      webapi    --use-minimal-apis   10            1       0         0
net10.0      webapi-controllers  webapi    --use-controllers    10            1       0         0
net10.0      mvc                 mvc       -                    10            4       0         0
net10.0      razorpages          webapp    -                    10            3       0         0
net8.0       webapi-minimal      webapi    --use-minimal-apis   10            1       0         0
net8.0       webapi-controllers  webapi    --use-controllers    10            1       0         0
net8.0       mvc                 mvc       -                    10            4       0         0
net8.0       razorpages          webapp    -                    10            3       0         0
